name: cursor-approve
description: Automatically approves Cursor's pending agent tool calls by invoking Cursor's own approval command.

cursorApprove.enabled.description: Poll for pending agent tool calls and approve them automatically.

cursorApprove.intervalMs.description: How often to check for a pending tool call, in milliseconds.

enumDescriptions: Approve only the current call, equivalent to pressing Run.
Approve and remember the command, equivalent to pressing Always Run.
cursorApprove.mode.description: Which of Cursor's approval commands to invoke.

cursorApprove.onlyWhenFocused.description: Only approve while this window has focus. Leave disabled for unattended operation.

cursorApprove.showStatusBarItem.description: Show a status bar item indicating whether automatic approval is active.

enumDescriptions: Fill the item using the theme's status bar warning colour.
Tint the text and icon with the theme's accent colour.
Use the default status bar colours with no highlight.
cursorApprove.statusBarStyle.markdownDescription:
How to highlight the status bar item while automatic approval is active.

`foreground` is the default because it is the only style that follows the theme's accent colour. VS Code allowlists exactly two status bar backgrounds, `statusBarItem.warningBackground` and `statusBarItem.errorBackground`, and colour customizations must be literal hex values, so a filled item cannot track an arbitrary accent.

Choose `background` for a filled item in your theme's warning colour. To recolour it, override that colour yourself:

```json
"workbench.colorCustomizations": {
  "statusBarItem.warningBackground": "#bd7ba2",
  "statusBarItem.warningForeground": "#ffffff"
}
```

cursorApprove.activeColor.markdownDescription: Colour used when `#cursorApprove.statusBarStyle#` is `foreground`. Accepts a [theme colour identifier](https://code.visualstudio.com/api/references/theme-color) such as `textLink.foreground`, which follows the current theme's accent, or a literal hex value such as `#bd7ba2`.
